text:
alex: Heads-up — I ran the flash-split tiler + paged attention variant on the nightly perf rig and hit a weird mem-bandwidth spike during KV-cache warmup. attaching a tiny snippet of the profiler.

maria: can you drop the profiler output and the exact bench command? curious if it's the tiler or the batching combo.

alex: pasted below. run: `./bench --model gpt-7B --kernel flashsplit_paged_tiler --batching heuristic=dynamic --kv-cache on --seq-len 1024 -n 500`

```
# perf-summary
iter 0..499: avg latency 42.7ms, p95 68.1ms, tokens/s 3200
sm_bandwidth: baseline ~620GB/s, spike window -> 985GB/s (30s window at iter 12-18)
gpu_occupancy: 62% steady, but SM shared mem stall rate increased from 4% -> 28% during spike
kv-cache hitrate: 0.72 -> 0.55 during spike (evictions observed)
batch composition: 40% short (<=128), 60% 1024
```

jin: that kv-cache drop + evictions + higher sm stall smells like pipeline stage contention — when the tiler picks larger sharedmem tiles it pushes more pressure on L2/KV prefetcher. did you run with the new eviction patch?

alex: not yet. I intentionally left eviction as default to reproduce the baseline. I also ran a microbench with homogeneous batches (all 1024) and the spike disappears, bandwidth normalizes ~630GB/s and kv hitrate stays 0.88.

maria: so it's an interaction between mixed-batching and tiler heuristics. two immediate ideas: 1) bias the dynamic batching heuristic to avoid mixing very short and very long in the same micro-batch; 2) lower sm tile size in flashsplit when `kv-cache` is enabled so prefetch/backpressure is reduced.

jin: agree. i can prototype a patch to the tiler that adds an occupancy-aware tile cap (cap_sm_words = max( sm_words, floor(occupancy_target * sm_capacity) )). quick patch should be low risk.

alex: please. can you also add a shortbench that simulates mixed-shot ratios? i'd like numbers for 10/90, 30/70, 50/50 short/long.

jin: will do. leaving local note: `bench/mixed_batch.py` to generate ratio sweep + produce token/s and kv hitrate.

sre-ops: if the canary shows >5% latency regressions revert. please add a log-forwarder label so we can grab nvprof dumps quickly.

nina: creating PERF ticket w/ reproduction steps, profiler snippet, and initial hypothesis. linking here: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3287 (add ops/bench artifacts) :sparkles:

alex: nice — i'll upload the `nvprof` snapshot and the mixed-batch numbers once jin finishes. thanks all. :thumbsup:
